title: POC Weekly — Microburst Hedging & Streaming Priorities
summary: Weekly sync to review microburst latency results, TTFT regressions observed on long seqs, decide kernel hedging approach and prioritize streaming fixes. Customer emphasized 99th percentile SLO and pref for VPC-friendly fallbacks. Agreed next steps: run two hedging experiments, share patched kernel metrics, align on pilot hard-stop date.
topics: TTFT regressions on long sequence lengths
next_steps: Redwood: run dual-path hedging experiment and send results (by 2026-06-25)
Customer: provide 24h sample traffic with seqlen histogram (by 2026-06-22)
Redwood: post kernel patch and perf spreadsheet to shared drive
Schedule follow-up demo for SRE stakeholders (tentative 2026-06-29)
action_items: Priya Singh - start dual-path hedging A/B (baseline vs priority queue) - due 2026-06-25
Noah Rivera - collate microburst traces and share annotated sheet - due 2026-06-20
Jon Park - supply 24h traffic seqlen histogram and top 50 prompts - due 2026-06-22
Liam O'Connor - run ingress load sim with 10% bursts and share logs - due 2026-06-24
header:
Date: 2026-06-18 | Time: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 42m
Attendees: Noah Rivera (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Ethan Morales (Redwood CSM); Maya Ramirez (ParcelWave CTO), Jon Park (ML Eng), Liam O'Connor (SRE), Sara Velez (Product)
transcript:
[00:00] Noah: ok thanks everyone for hopping on, quick check-in today focused on the microburst hedging experiments, streaming handshake, and that TTFT blip we saw on the long sequences. um Maya, you want to kick off?
[01:00] Maya: yeah thanks Noah, uh we ran the end-to-end test overnight with the default hedging config from last week. overall average token latency looked fine but the 99th jumped to ~1.9s on seqlens >5k, which is above our target 1.2s, so that's the main worry.
[02:00] Priya: when you say 5k, is that concatenated user history plus system prompt or purely generated length?
[03:00] Jon: mostly user history, we prepend ~1.2k tokens on avg, but there are edge cases where historic context hits 4k, then new prompt is 1k so total crosses 5k. it's not common but happens in top 3% traces.
[04:00] Noah: okay that helps; so distribution is heavy tail. we expected some variance, but the TTFT regression on long seqlen is probably kernel selection and KV cache pressure. Priya, quick synopsis?
[05:00] Priya: yeah so from profiling the runtime we saw two things: kernel fallbacks for attention when seqlen>4096 cause additional memcpy and reformat, and KV cache eviction churn during continuous batching. the combination spikes first-byte.
[06:00] Jon: uh huh we saw that in our logs too — there were spikes aligned with garbage-collect-like events in the cache. sometimes called K-V cash in the logs, the transcription had that funny typo earlier, ha.
[07:00] Liam: question from infra side, are those kernel fallbacks on our side or within the redwood runtime? is there a knob we can flip in our config?
[08:00] Priya: they're runtime decisions; we pick optimized kernels per seqlen and backend, but we can force kernel hedging — run two candidate kernels in parallel for the first N tokens and pick the earliest response. that's the dual-path hedging approach.
[09:00] Maya: hedging sounds expensive, cost is a factor, but SLO is top priority. what's the expected cost multiplier?
[10:00] Priya: depends — dual-path for first 64 tokens adds roughly 1.1x token compute for those requests, but hedging only on candidate long-seqlen requests reduces net impact. we can also make it adaptive by sample rate.
[11:00] Noah: also there's priority queueing hedging — keep a small low-latency path pre-warmed for microbursts and push lower-priority batch jobs to a secondary queue. cheaper than full dual run but needs capacity reservation.
[12:00] Jon: reservation is okay if we can bound burst percentiles; our ops team can carve 10% capacity for low-latency lane.
[13:00] Ethan: note: last week's test used baseline two-queue with warmup disabled; that might explain misses on cold microbursts.
[14:00] Priya: streaming side — handshake was adding 120-200ms in library handshakes when chunking threshold was 64 tokens. increasing chunk to 128 reduced handshake calls but increased TTFT slightly for short outputs. it's a tradeoff.
[15:00] Sara: product note — some clients require near-immediate first token for chat UX, so we can't lose more than 100ms on TTFT for short messages.
[16:00] Priya: we can use adaptive chunking: if expected generation length <32, stream immediately with small chunk; if >128, buffer until a chunk is ready. but detection needs a cheap estimate; we can send a quick heuristic from the client.
[17:00] Noah: about observability, we still have gaps — 99th traces don't consistently show kernel decision label; add a tag to the trace that says kernel=optimA or fallbackB. can you add that Priya?
[18:00] Priya: yes will add kernel label to spans and export the raw microburst traces to the sheet. link will be in the notes: https://redwood.ai/poc/parcelwave/trace-06-18.
[19:00] Jon: another datapoint: hedging seemed to help on 95th but not 99th in the prior run, maybe because the worst spikes were caused by eviction stalls, not kernel latency.
[20:00] Priya: good point — we need to differentiate eviction stalls vs compute path stalls. eviction shows up as long memcpy in profile; compute stalls show as long op time. we will annotate.
[21:00] Liam: about KV cache, we hit memory pressure at peak; curious if quantized model variants would ease memory and reduce swaps?
[22:00] Priya: quantization helps memory but can change kernel choice; it's a separate axis. we can try q4_0 for the long-seqlen path and keep q8_0 for low-latency lane. that may complicate routing but possible.
[23:00] Maya: do we have a simple routing config in the console to send long seqlen to q4 variant? or is that a policy we need Redwood to add?
[24:00] Noah: we can set a request router rule: if seqlen_estimate > 4096 route to q4_variant; if low-latency tag present route to warm lane. Priya can draft the rule.
[25:00] Priya: will draft and share. also propose two experiments this week: A) dual-path hedging for first 64 tokens on sampled long requests, B) queue-priority with 10% reserved pre-warmed pods.
[26:00] Jon: Jon: how will success be measured? 99th improvement below 1.2s and no more than 10% cost increase?
[27:00] Noah: yes agreed — primary metric 99th token latency <=1.2s, secondary cost delta <10% for production profile.
[28:00] Ethan: for the experiment we should run at least 24h of representative traffic with preserved burstiness; can Redwood run the injected bursts?
[29:00] Priya: yes we'll provide a load harness. quick note — need sample prompts so the model path reflects actual length. Jon, please share top 50 prompts.
[30:00] Jon: will share; one small ask — can you include the packet-level ingress timelines in the traces? our SRE uses that to correlate upstream spikes.
[31:00] Priya: yes we'll include ingress timestamps and annotate spikes. also we'll add an event marker when kernel fallback happens.
[32:00] Liam: we had issues last run where streaming handshake timeouts were due to proxy idle timeouts in our VPC; we need to coordinate with infra and Redwood's keepalive.
[33:00] Noah: good flag — Redwood can extend keepalive on streaming connections for this pilot; we will recommend 90s keepalive for pilot.
[34:00] Maya: about security/compliance, small ask: can we get audit log snippets showing request ids for hedged requests? our audit team wants to verify no request duplication externally visible.
[35:00] Ethan: we can surface request_id parent/child mapping in audit logs if hedging duplicates initial requests; we'll ensure it's internal-only and not double-billed in the usage report.
[36:00] Priya: quick technical aside — hedging duplicate suppression is implemented at the router layer but we still show a single logical request id; physical ops may show two worker traces but they are collapsed in billing.
[37:00] Sara: product ask — if hedging changes token ordering occasionally in streaming, will that affect our downstream transcript merge?
[38:00] Priya: normally we pick earliest streaming chunks and discard the slower path, sequence remains monotonic. we'll add a small sequence-checker in the client to accept only strictly increasing chunk offsets.
[39:00] Jon: curious about the kernel patch you mentioned — is that a Redwood runtime change or a vendor kernel update?
[40:00] Priya: it's a Redwood runtime tweak to reduce memcpy by reusing a pre-allocated staging buffer for attention reformat. small change but low-risk; we'll run canary.
[41:00] Noah: next practical items: Priya runs the two experiments and shares results by 6/25; Jon shares prompts and histogram by 6/22; Noah will post annotated traces by 6/20. any other blockers?
[42:00] Maya: one: budget approval might lag. if hedging looks like 12% cost we may need exec signoff. we'll flag early.
[43:00] Noah: understood; we'll include a cost projection table. Priya, Ethan, please coordinate.
[44:00] Priya: quick note — we'll include dashboard tiles for kernel decisions, eviction events, TTFT by seqlen bucket.
[45:00] Jon: thanks — that will help SRE triage.
[46:00] Noah: ok wrapping up, recap next steps and owners, we'll send minutes and links. thanks everyone.
[47:00] Maya: thanks all.
[41:50] (call ended)
